sense: owed; payable on a set day

terms.gloss: owe; in the passive, be owed, be due
evidence: Cic. Att. 14.18.1: Kal. Jān. dēbuit, adhūc nōn solvit
Cic. Fam. 3.5.4: pecūnia … quae mihi ex pūblicā permūtātiōne dēbētur
terms.comment: “It is due” is the passive, dēbētur; what is due, dēbitum.

terms.gloss: the due date, the day set
terms.grammar: noun, fifth declension; feminine in this sense
evidence: Caes. BG 6.33.4: quam ad diem eī legiōnī … dēbērī frūmentum sciēbat
Caes. BG 1.8.3: ubi ea diēs quam cōnstituerat cum lēgātīs vēnit
terms.comment: A day fixed in advance, for a payment, a meeting or a hearing, is feminine (Lewis & Short; see day).

phrases.latin: Kal. Jān. dēbuit, adhūc nōn solvit
phrases.english: the money was due on the first of January, and he still hasn’t paid

phrases.latin: quam ad diem eī legiōnī quae in praesidiō relinquēbātur dēbērī frūmentum sciēbat
phrases.english: the day on which, as he knew, corn was due to the legion left on guard

debeo.html: With an infinitive, dēbeō speaks of a duty, never of what is merely expected to happen: Lewis & Short, in classical prose always of moral necessity.

sources: Lewis & Short: debeo · Lewis & Short: dies
